mainEntity.name: How do AI customer support workflows actually work from first message to resolution?

acceptedAnswer.text: An AI-assisted support workflow can classify incoming questions, retrieve approved information, draft or send a response, record the interaction, and route exceptions to a person. The prompt is only one part of the system; the workflow also needs connected tools, permissions, reliable source material, and review rules. Context: Run My AI Biz presents specialized assistants as adaptable blueprints, not identical software products. A support assistant may therefore need separate instructions for triage, drafting, escalation, and reporting. Key factors: - where customer messages arrive - which system contains account or order data - what actions require approval - how unresolved conversations are tracked. Practical guidance: Map the real process from incoming message to resolution, including failed integrations and unusual cases. Then define the assistant’s allowed sources and actions before connecting accounts. This educational, human-directed approach helps owners understand what the system can actually do.
acceptedAnswer.description: The workflow usually classifies the message, finds approved information, drafts or sends a reply, records the interaction, and escalates exceptions. It also needs integrations, permissions, source documents, and clear approval rules; a prompt alone does not create a working support system.
